olivia (eng-platform): Heads up — we're seeing a consistent mismatch between the serving runtime token accounting and the observability-derived cost estimates for inference requests that hit the prefix/KV cache. Example: runtime shows 0.2 tokens billed (cache hit), obs pipeline attributes ~0.6 token-equivalent cost. Anyone seen this?

sam (runtime): Yeah. Short version: runtime charges are per-decoded token served from model execution while our telemetry currently imputes cost based on request metadata + model variant average. Cache hits reduce GPU work but obs doesn't know it happened.

matt (infra): Can we add an explicit signal from the runtime into the telemetry envelope for cache-hit vs cache-miss? A small boolean would make aggregation straightforward.

raj (sre): That'd be ideal but caution: adding a high-cardinality field (e.g., kernel_variant, kernel_id, quant_level) multiplies metrics/trace cardinality. We need a plan to avoid explosion.

olivia (eng-platform): Tradeoffs I've sketched: (1) emit minimal flags from runtime (cache_hit: true/false, exec_tokens: int), (2) keep runtime opaque and compute cost on ingest via sampling + model-profile heuristics, or (3) emit a compact cost_hint field (coarse bucket: low/med/high) to avoid exact numbers. Thoughts?

maria (billing): From billing accuracy POV, (1) with exec_tokens is best. We can reconcile invoices with near-100% fidelity. But I'm worried about payload size and telemetry cardinality.

sam (runtime): exec_tokens is cheap to compute — we already know how many decode ops happen. The data we would attach per-request is two small ints/bools. If we compress/envelope it as a small bitfield we can keep size down.

matt (infra): Implementation options at ingest: A) accept new fields and index them as low-cardinality facets; B) sink them to a separate high-throughput timeseries store for cost accounting only; C) only emit on sampled requests and extrapolate. Each has pros/cons: A simplest for queries; B reduces pressure on observability index; C saves bandwidth but loses per-request fidelity for small customers.

raj (sre): Also need to consider backpressure when runtime emits extras at high TPS. If we add flags to every request envelope, edge proxies may hit size limits. We should measure 99p envelope size with and without fields.

olivia (eng-platform): Quick benchmark idea: instrument a canary pool to emit exec_tokens and cache_hit into a reserved header X-RW-Exec-Tokens (base64 packed) and route to our ingest-test topic. Then run workload for 1 hour and measure ingest volume, index cardinality, query perf.

sam (runtime): I can ship the header and a tiny serializer this week. Suggest using bitfield: 1 bit cache_hit, 1 bit model_variant_small_id (up to 4), 14 bits exec_tokens (up to 16k), rest reserved. Then base64 to avoid breaking proxies.

matt (infra): On the ingest side I'll spin up a separate consumer that writes to a denormalized cost topic and a compact timeseries. We can avoid altering the main trace index for now. If results look good, we can add low-cardinality derived fields into the obsv index: cache_hit:boolean and cost_bucket:string.

maria (billing): After we have per-request exec_tokens we can reconcile for last-month invoices and quantify the delta. Please tag me on the canary results.

raj (sre): Also propose an eventual fallback: if we find carriers of high-cardinality like kernel_variant cause blowup, we should prefer probabilistic sampling of full-variant details and supply aggregated histograms per-rollout-period instead.

olivia (eng-platform): Action items: (1) sam -> ship header+serializer to canary (ETA Tue), (2) matt -> consumer + compact cost topic + dashboard (ETA Thu), (3) raj -> envelope-size/backpressure test & probe (ETA Thu), (4) maria -> reconcile plan once data available. I'll own the tech-check doc.

sam (runtime): I'll paste the serializer proto here once I push:
```
// v0 exec bitfield layout (16 bits)
// bit0: cache_hit
// bit1-2: model_variant_small (00 default, 01 v1, 10 v2, 11 reserved)
// bit3-15: exec_tokens (unsigned)
```

matt (infra): Small note: ingestion consumer should tag messages with ingest-shard id so we can measure cross-shard skew in costs.

olivia (eng-platform): Agreed. One more open question: do we want to backfill historical traces with an estimated adjustment? That would help billing but is heavier.

maria (billing): Backfill only if delta > 5% for the last billing period. Let's measure first.

raj (sre): Cool. If canary shows envelope size growth < 8% and no QoS regressions, I'm +1 for widening rollout with the denormalized cost topic approach.

ingest-bot: New consumer created: obsv-cost-v0 (topic) by matt. Link: https://kafka.internal/obsv-cost-v0 (internal).

olivia (eng-platform): Thanks all — I'll create the tech-check doc and a short RFC with these options + benchmarks. Ping me for the doc: /search tech-check cache-cost.

sam (runtime): Will follow up with PR for header and unit tests.

matt (infra): I'll post the dashboard link in this thread when ready.

maria (billing): Thanks — will standby for reconciliation numbers.

olivia (eng-platform): End of thread for now. We'll reconvene after canary data. :thumbsup:
